newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS-Coffee volatilities firm, cocoa drifts.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS-Coffee volatilities firm, cocoa drifts.

text.p: Coffee remained the main focus of LIFFE soft options this week as volatilities firmed slightly but premiums on cocoa eased.
Interest in coffee mainly centred on some January and March positions following trade buying to protect the downside risk.
Trading on Thursday was dominated by fence-trades, or "Combo" under the LIFFE badge, as buyers tried to defend the downside.
These include buying the March $1,250 put and selling the $1,550 call and buying the January $1,250 put and selling the $1,600 call.

Coffee futures seesawed in volatile trade this week, lifted by news of a sharp drawdown in U.S. certified stocks and prolonged truckers' strike in Colombia but later pulled back as the 11-day strike came to an end.
But traders noted as long as the nearby tightness prevails, the market would remain highly nervous.
Spot contract on both the New York and London markets remained at a wide premium to the second position, reflecting the nearby tight supplies.
But traders expect the hefty spread would fall in the coming weeks as Central and South American supplies reach the western markets.
Second-month January on the LIFFE contract rose to a high of $1,433 a tonne on Tuesday before easing off to trade at around $1,380 late on Friday.
In the options pit, traders said the January $1,400 put, which has by far the biggest open interest at 1,500 lots, was also the spotlight as players rolled down their expired November positions.
Reflecting the futures market movement, volatitilies were a tick firmer this week with January at-the-money calls and puts trading at around 30-31 percent against 27-29 percent last week.
March calls however remained at 24-25 percent.
Options turnover reached over 3,000 lots so far this week.
Cocoa options were thinly traded and traders said the March calls were traded at implied volatility of around 19.5 percent which was seen as a fair value.
But one trade house said of interest this week was a sizeable bid in the March 1,075 stg call strike where 1,000 lots were bid for at 10 stg, an implied volatility of 18 percent.
"The bid was a little on the cheap side and thus the market believed the bid was shown only to provide short-term support to the price level," it said.
Cocoa futures slipped out of their range this week on technical-related factors.

There were little fundamental news driving the market. Traders said news Ivory Coast kept its cocoa farm-gate price unchanged at 320 CFA francs for the new 1996/97 marketing campaign was within expectation.
The market is now awaiting word on the Ivorian arrivals to help gauge the size of the new crop. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
